children: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (NSE:HAL) reported Q1FY27 revenue of Rs 5,515 crore and net profit Rs 1,590 crore with a Rs 2,54,538 crore order book, while ROH arm yields steady revenue but LCA Mk-1A deliveries face GE engine-linked execution risk and government pressure to resolve delays.
: HAL Q1FY27: revenue Rs 5,515 crore (+14.4% YoY), net profit Rs 1,590 crore (+14.9% YoY); order book at Rs 2,54,538 crore; reiterates FY27 revenue growth guidance of 10–12%.
: HAL's ROH arm generates about ₹20,000 crore yearly, driven by maintenance contracts for Indian Air Force and Navy aircraft, providing a steady, recurring revenue stream for the company
: HAL faces execution risk on LCA Mk‑1A deliveries due to dependence on GE Aerospace engine supplies; past engine delays caused liquidated damages and pushed project timelines.

: HAL expects delivery of 10 LCA Mk-1A fighters by March 2026 after receiving 10 F404 engines; GE to supply 12 more F404 engines by December. Recent handovers: LCA Mk-1A FOC trainers, HTT-40, Dhruv NG.
Rajnath Singh Urges Timely Tejas Delivery
: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh warned Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) over Tejas LCA Mk-1A delivery delays, citing potential capability gaps and higher costs, and urged prompt resolution.
: HAL rallied after DAC approved Advanced Light Helicopters procurement, then corrected. Traders note the DAC approval triggered the earlier upward move in HAL shares.
LCA Tejas Trainers And Dhruv NG Handovers
: HAL delivered final two LCA Tejas FOC twin‑seat trainers and HTT‑40 basic trainer to Indian Air Force; also handed over Dhruv NG helicopters to Pawan Hans in Bengaluru.
HAL Shares Move On Delivery News
: HAL shares traded near Rs 4,876 on NSE, rising about 2% intraday after a delivery-related announcement; intraday price movement reflected the delivery news.
